Current_Trend: ACCELERATING — employer costs +30% from GLP-1s; claims rose from 6.9% of Rx costs (2023) to 10.5% (2025). Medicare GLP-1 Bridge July-Dec 2026 ($50 copay). BALANCE Model Medicare Part D Jan 2027. Medicaid BALANCE Model May 2026 for opt-in states.
Employer_Impact: 64% of large employers say "significant" impact; 49% of 500+ firms covering for weight loss (up from ~43%); 66% of 20,000+ firms; Medicare Bridge: $50/mo outside Part D benefit
Consumer_Impact: $349-$499/mo list for self-pay (unchanged); Medicare Bridge $50 copay but NOT credited to $2,100 OOP cap; LIS enrollees don't get subsidized rate
Magnitude: Estimated 14% premium increase if universally covered; Rx trend 11-12% in 2026 driven largely by GLP-1s
K_Shape_Note: Top 40%: can access via employer coverage or self-pay; now also via Medicare Bridge ($50). Bottom 60%: can't afford $350-500/mo; Medicaid BALANCE opt-in May 2026 (limited states); LIS Medicare enrollees excluded from Bridge subsidized rate — access gap persists for poorest seniors.
Source: KFF Employer Benefits 2025; Mercer National Survey of Employer-Sponsored Health Plans 2025; PwC Behind the Numbers 2026; CMS Medicare GLP-1 Bridge 2026; KFF Quick Take Medicare GLP-1 Bridge
Notes: [Updated 2026-04-17] GLP-1 remains SINGLE BIGGEST 2026 cost driver. Medicare Bridge (Jul-Dec 2026) is a meaningful new access signal for Medicare population but with important limitations (outside Part D OOP cap; LIS exclusion). Employer coverage expanding (49% at 500+ firms). Biosimilar competition ~2032. BALANCE Model Jan 2027 is the more permanent Medicare solution.

Current_Trend: PERSISTENT — specialty drugs now >50% of pharmacy spend despite <5% of Rx volume; new launches at $500K-$4M/yr
Employer_Impact: Per-patient specialty costs $70K-$200K+; stop-loss thresholds being hit more frequently
Consumer_Impact: High deductibles met faster on specialty → OOP max exposure; adherence challenges at any copay
Magnitude: 10-15% of total healthcare cost growth annually; growing pipeline means persistent upward pressure
K_Shape_Note: Bottom 60%: cannot afford specialty copays even with coverage; worse cancer outcomes documented. Top 40%: better coverage but stop-loss and premium pass-through increasing.
Source: IQVIA National Trends 2025; Segal 2026 Cost Trend
Notes: Gene therapies and oncology biologics pipeline will keep specialty pressure persistent through the decade.

Current_Trend: STRUCTURAL — >75% of hospital markets now highly concentrated; consolidated systems charge 20-40% more
Employer_Impact: Employer/insurer cost shifting; narrow networks compressing access options
Consumer_Impact: Higher facility fees, less network choice, surprise billing exposure (ground ambulance unprotected)
Magnitude: Major driver of hospital price growth (~3.5% YoY) exceeding general inflation
K_Shape_Note: Bottom 60%: fewer low-cost access options when systems consolidate; rural communities lose critical access hospitals. Top 40%: can pay but premium pass-through rising.
Notes: PE acquisition of physician groups accelerating. DoJ antitrust enforcement limited against hospital mergers. Structural.

Current_Trend: PERSISTENT — avg deductible $1,886 (+17% since 2020, +43% over decade); HDHPs now cover 57% of workers
Employer_Impact: Cost shift from employers to employees; HDHPs marketed as "consumer-directed"
Consumer_Impact: $1,886 deductible = 3% of $60K median income before first claim; OOP max up to $9,450; 72% face $3,000+ OOP max
Magnitude: Every dollar of deductible increase = direct consumer cost burden; $1 trillion+ in annual cost-shifting estimated
K_Shape_Note: Bottom 60%: can't fund HSA; deductible is effective uninsurance. 53% of small-firm workers face $2,000+. Top 40%: can fund HSA but OOP maximums increasing.
Notes: Core structural driver. Without policy reversal, will continue compounding. +43% over decade is disqualifying for access.

Current_Trend: MODERATING from 2022-23 crisis peak; travel nurse market normalized; but nursing vacancies remain elevated
Employer_Impact: Labor is 50-60% of hospital costs; moderation helped margins recover to 1.3% median
Consumer_Impact: Indirectly: labor stabilization may slow consumer cost growth; but hospitals need margins to reinvest
Magnitude: Labor was 2022-23 primary driver; now moderated; replaced by GLP-1 and volume as primary drivers
K_Shape_Note: Affects rural hospitals disproportionately (46% negative margins) — closures hurt bottom cohort access
Source: Kaufman Hall Flash Report Dec 2025; FITCH hospital outlook
Notes: Travel nurse crisis resolved but permanent nursing shortage persists. Next labor disruption (union contracts, AI-driven workforce changes) could re-accelerate.

Current_Trend: ACUTE 2026 TRIGGER — enhanced subsidies expired Dec 31, 2025; premiums +114% avg for subsidized enrollees
Employer_Impact: Employers: indirect (uninsured shift to ER → uncompensated care costs)
Consumer_Impact: 9% of ACA enrollees now uninsured; 4.8M total expected coverage loss; premiums doubled
Magnitude: New acute trigger: 1.2M fewer enrolled, 4.8M uninsured, premium shock for those staying
K_Shape_Note: Self-employed, gig workers, early retirees disproportionately on ACA — middle-income households. Bottom 60%: Medicaid/CHIP less affected. ACA cliff hits $30K-$80K income band.
Source: CMS 2026 enrollment; CNBC/KFF Mar 2026; Urban Institute
Notes: This is the most acute 2026 trigger. Congress unlikely to reinstate (KFF poll: 67% say "wrong thing" not to extend). Will contribute to deferred care and medical debt surge in 2026.

Current_Trend: COMPLETING — unwinding removed 25M from Medicaid; enrollment stabilized ~10M above pre-pandemic; proposed budget cuts risk further loss
Employer_Impact: Medicaid budget cuts being debated in Congress; expansion rollbacks proposed in some states
Consumer_Impact: Medicaid enrollees = lowest income, highest healthcare need; coverage loss = immediate OOP exposure
Magnitude: 25M removed (31% termination rate); further cuts could add millions more uninsured
K_Shape_Note: Direct bottom 60% impact — Medicaid is primary coverage for lowest income households. Expansion states median margin +3pp vs non-expansion. Rural communities most exposed.
Notes: Budget reconciliation 2026 may include Medicaid work requirements or per-capita caps. Watch for federal policy developments.

Current_Trend: PERSISTENT — ongoing regulatory scrutiny but PBM practices unchanged; vertical integration at CVS/Cigna/UnitedHealth deepening
Employer_Impact: PBM rebates benefit insurer, not always passed to consumer; formulary restrictions increasing access barriers
Consumer_Impact: Rebate pass-through debate: estimated $30-50B in rebates not reaching patients; step therapy delays
Magnitude: Estimated 6-10% of drug cost is PBM spread/arbitrage; regulatory action limited
K_Shape_Note: Bottom 60%: less able to navigate formularies, access specialty meds, or use manufacturer coupons. Top 40%: better literacy/advocacy, but still exposed.
Source: FTC PBM Report 2024; Congressional scrutiny ongoing
Notes: FTC vs. PBM lawsuits pending. Legislative reform possible but slow. Structural inefficiency, not crisis-level.
